result.instructions: Tailrace console management plane. Read tools (list/get/compile, ddl_draft, backfill_status, apply_dry_run) are always available. Write tools (create_pipeline, deploy_pipeline, pause_resume_pipeline, trigger_backfill, ddl_execute, ddl_evolve, apply) are ENABLED; every write call must also pass "confirm": true. All calls are audited as actor mcp:<client>.

tools.description:
GET /api/datasources — `GET /api/datasources?type=&layer=` (§4.2; `layer` accepted for form
compatibility — the v1 model has no layer dimension).

type.description: Registry type filter; omit for all

tools.name: list_datasources

tools.description:
GET /api/pipelines/{id}/stats — `GET /api/pipelines/{id}/stats` — engine stats proxy, body verbatim; the
engine's own ok:false ("not registered") passes through on 200 for the
frontend's degrade branch (§4.5).
tools.name: get_pipeline_stats

tools.description:
GET /api/pipelines/{id}/logs — `GET /api/pipelines/{id}/logs?lines=200&after_seq=N` — SSE bridge over
the engine's cursor API: initial `tail=1&limit` (clamped 50..500), then
1.5s `after_seq` polling; keepalive every 15s; session ends at 300s or
after 5 consecutive engine failures (eof event, §4.5). A client-supplied
`after_seq>0` seeds the cursor (log continuation on reconnect — no tail
replay; the engine only returns entries past that global seq).
tools.name: get_pipeline_logs

tools.description:
POST /api/pipelines/compile — `POST /api/pipelines/compile` — local compile via the embedded
tailrace-parser (§4.6: offline editor diagnostics). Diagnostics ride a
400 whose body is the compile shape (not the generic envelope — §4.5's
own 400 example).

tools.description:
POST /api/pipelines/{id}/deploy — `POST /api/pipelines/{id}/deploy` — plan push-down with auto-assignment
(preferred eligible → fewest running → lowest id, §4.5) and the full plan
body per §4.5/engine B.2. Engine `ok:false` records DEPLOY_FAILED and
returns 502. T-A7: the snapshot's partial-column declarations are
re-gated against their registered sinks (400 diagnostics, same as
publish — a pre-A7 snapshot or a moved key model never flips into partial
mode unchecked), then a plan with partial-column sinks is checked live
for a schema change in flight on each such sink (409
SCHEMA_CHANGE_IN_PROGRESS; FE unreachable → 502 UNAVAILABLE).

tools.description:
POST /api/pipelines/{id}/backfill — `POST /api/pipelines/{id}/backfill` (blueprint §7.3): preview or enqueue
a bounded replay. `dryRun:true` answers the job-shape preview
(jobId/estimatedRows/labelPrefix) with ZERO side effects — no job row,
no audit, no execution. `dryRun:false` creates a pending job row (the
console-store migration 02 table), audits the acceptance and spawns the
console-side executor: bf-{jobId} ledger namespace + deterministic
labels (W2), main-pipeline cursors untouched in every outcome.

confirm.description: Explicit acknowledgement of a state-changing call; rejected unless exactly true.

tools.name: trigger_backfill

tools.description:
POST /api/datasources/{id}/tables/{db}/{table}/ddl/draft — `POST /api/datasources/{id}/tables/{db}/{table}/ddl/draft` (T-A1 ①+②):
the registered columns through the pure generator — full DDL text, key
model + reason, key column highlight with its 「猜测」 flag, partition
candidate. Read-only (nothing touches Doris, nothing is audited); the
body carries the human's round-two confirmations, if any.

columnTypes.description: Per-column type overrides [name, vocabulary type]; steers this draft only

keyModel.description: Key-model override; the recommendation stands when absent

partition.description: true = confirmed candidate; false = dropped (no PARTITION BY)

tools.name: ddl_draft

tools.description:
POST /api/datasources/{id}/tables/{db}/{table}/ddl/execute — `POST /api/datasources/{id}/tables/{db}/{table}/ddl/execute` (T-A1 ③+④):
run the echoed draft through `mysql_exec` once the key model is
confirmed. Gate first — `keyModel` absent/unknown, `ddl` absent, or a
`ddl` whose key clause contradicts `keyModel` → 422 before any
connection is opened. The attempt is audited either way: the full DDL
text and wall time on success, the Doris message on failure (which is
also what the 502 carries, verbatim — §7.2 ④ 失败原样回传). Statements
run as sent: no rewriting, no allowlist — the confirmed text is the gate.

confirm.description: Explicit acknowledgement of a state-changing call; rejected unless exactly true.

ddl.description: The draft text echoed back verbatim

tools.name: ddl_execute

tools.description:
POST /api/datasources/{id}/tables/{db}/{table}/ddl/evolve — T-A7 mutex, evolve side: a partial-update pipeline deployed on the table
(its INSERT column list makes every load a partial load, which Doris
refuses mid-schema-change) → 409 PARTIAL_UPDATE_ACTIVE naming the
pipelines, before anything touches Doris — stop them first. The gate is
on the TABLE, not on the diff: it fires even when the live table would
turn out to need nothing, because telling a no-op from an ADD takes the
DESC, and the conservative answer costs one stop/redeploy while the
other answer costs a pipeline failing at 3am.

tools.description:
POST /api/apply — `POST /api/apply` — idempotent upsert of the declaration file. Objects
that already match are left byte-untouched (no status flip, no
generation bump, no audit row); only real drift writes. Never deletes:
removals from the file become orphan entries in the response. Audited
per actual write plus one APPLY summary row.

inputSchema.description: Declaration file (docs/ops/pipeline-file.md). Every section is optional; a PRESENT section is the declared full set of that kind — console objects it does not name are reported as orphans, never deleted. Objects are identified by business key (datasource name / datasource+db+table / pipeline name), never by numeric id.

confirm.description: Explicit acknowledgement of a state-changing call; rejected unless exactly true.

datasources.description: DatasourceUpsertBody entries: name, type, connJson, optional username/password (blank password keeps the stored credential)

pipelines.description: PipelineUpsertBody entries: name, sqlContent, dsMapping (alias -> datasource NAME or id), checkpointMs, preferredNodeId, config

tables.description: TableRegisterBody entries plus `datasource` — the owning datasource NAME (numeric ids are still accepted)
